anchor: ATO Phase 1 — per-sector designation of the ONE ratio operators should watch as their headline benchmark. Adopted from the ATO Small Business Benchmarks framework (atogovau Benchmarks A-Z). For every sector we pick one of cogs / labor / rent / motor_vehicle / total_expenses. The picker rule: cogs_share >= 0.25 -> cogs; labor_share >= 0.40 -> labor; else -> total_expenses. Two exceptions: transport_small -> motor_vehicle (the vehicle is the business), hospitality -> total_expenses (split fixed/variable cost makes any single ratio noisy).
convention: Source of truth for key_benchmark assignments. Mirrored into industry_cost_profile_v1.json for the cost-engine's convenience; this file is canonical.

key_benchmark_definitions.cogs: Cost of sales (variable inputs ex-labour) as a percentage of revenue. The variable cost moves directly with sales, making it the most accurate predictor of true turnover.
key_benchmark_definitions.labor: Total labour cost (wages + benefits + payroll tax) as a percentage of revenue. The most useful gauge for service businesses where people ARE the product.
key_benchmark_definitions.rent: Lease and occupancy cost as a percentage of revenue. Only chosen for businesses where location density is a dominant pricing factor.
key_benchmark_definitions.motor_vehicle: Vehicle, fuel, maintenance, depreciation as a percentage of revenue. Used for transport businesses where the vehicle IS the operational unit.
key_benchmark_definitions.total_expenses: Sum of all operating expenses as a percentage of revenue. The fallback when no single line dominates the cost structure.

food_drink.rationale: Food and beverage cost moves directly with sales. The most predictive ratio for true turnover.

hospitality.rationale: Hotels and lodging carry split fixed and variable cost; total expense vs revenue is the cleanest read.

beauty_wellness.rationale: Stylists and therapists ARE the product. Labour share against revenue is the right gauge.

retail_shops.rationale: Inventory cost tracks revenue directly. The classic retail benchmark.

professional_services.rationale: Lawyers, accountants, consultants sell time. Labour share answers whether you are charging enough.

creative_media.rationale: Designers, agencies, production houses bill labour. The labour ratio is the leverage gauge.

software_tech.rationale: Engineering payroll is the dominant line. Labour vs revenue is the unit-economics signal.

construction.rationale: Materials and subcontractor passthrough drive the P&L. Cost of sales is the most accurate predictor.

trades_home.rationale: Mixed materials and labour; total expense vs revenue captures both sides cleanly.

repair.rationale: Parts plus labour in a roughly equal mix. Total expense is the most stable benchmark.

health_clinics.rationale: Practitioner payroll dominates the cost stack. Labour vs revenue gauges practice efficiency.

education_instruction.rationale: Instructor cost is the operational lever. Labour-to-revenue tracks teaching utilisation.

events_entertainment.rationale: Event costs are project-based and volatile. Total expense vs revenue is the cleanest aggregate.

cultural.rationale: Galleries, museums, performing arts run mixed economics. Total expense is the most stable cut.

pet_services.rationale: Groomers, trainers, walkers are paid for time. Labour vs revenue is the throughput gauge.

real_estate.rationale: Commission economics make any single ratio noisy. Total expense vs revenue is the cleanest aggregate.

transport_small.rationale: The vehicle IS the business. Motor vehicle share vs revenue is the central operational ratio.

manufacturing_artisan.rationale: Raw materials are the dominant input. Cost of sales tracks the production economics directly.

heavy_industry.rationale: Material throughput drives revenue. Cost of sales is the most accurate turnover predictor.

mining_energy.rationale: Extracted material valued at sales prices. Cost of sales is the natural benchmark.

farming_food_production.rationale: Crop and livestock input costs drive the P&L. Cost of sales is the most reliable yield indicator.

telecom_broadcasting.rationale: Capex-heavy mixed economics. Total expense vs revenue is the cleanest single ratio.

finance_corp.rationale: Talent cost is the dominant lever. Labour vs revenue is the productivity benchmark.

higher_ed_hospitals.rationale: Faculty and clinician payroll dominate. Labour vs revenue tracks institutional efficiency.

other_local.rationale: Mixed local services. Total expense vs revenue is the cleanest cross-industry benchmark.
